rationale: This 1975 legal study examines federal and state statutory schemes governing disclosure of government-held information versus protection of personal privacy. It does not concern household or community water or sanitation service access (C1 = no, C4 = no) and presents a doctrinal statutory analysis rather than empirical research or a systematic review (C3 = no). Excluded under E01 (wrong topic).
plain_vs_narrow_note: Both narrow and plain Criterion 2 readings result in exclusion because the record is a doctrinal legal analysis of public-records disclosure and personal-privacy statutes with no connection to water or sanitation services (E01).

evidence_quotes.quote: Government Information and the Rights of Citizens
Clearly, the interests in maximizing disclosure of government-held information and minimizing the handling and dissemination of unnecessary or inaccurate personal information can conflict.
The contours of this conflict, only intimated herein, will doubtless become more bold with the maturation of the opposing statutory schemes.
